coachingPoints: The hedge must be hard and flat — a soft hedge helps nobody
The hedging big recovers on a sprint, not a jog — the roll man is his responsibility
The guard must get through the screen skinny and recover to the ball
Only hedge with bigs who can move; a slow big hedging is a layup drill
Use the hedge as a change-up, not a full-game diet — offenses adjust
commonMistakes: Hedging soft — the ball handler splits it and the defense is broken
The big hedging and then jogging back — the roller gets a free dunk
Hedging without weak-side help behind it — no tag means no recovery
The guard failing to get through — two defenders on the ball and nobody on the roll
description: Hedging ball screens: the big jumps out hard to stop the ball, then sprints back — timing, angles, and recovery.
gameSituations: Against a great ball handler you want to get the ball out of his hands
Late clock when you need to disrupt the offense's timing
As a change-up coverage to confuse a pick & roll heavy team
When your big is mobile enough to show high and recover

howTo.detail: As the ball handler comes off the screen, the screener's defender jumps out hard and high — above the level of the screen — getting square to the ball handler and stopping his momentum cold.
howTo.title: Big jumps out hard on the ball

howTo.detail: The hedging big stays with the ball handler for one or two dribbles, forcing him to retreat or pick up the ball. The goal is disruption, not a steal.
howTo.title: Contain for a two-count

howTo.detail: Meanwhile the on-ball defender fights over or under the screen and recovers to the ball handler. The moment the guard is back on the ball, the big's job is done.
howTo.title: Guard recovers to the ball

howTo.detail: The instant the guard recovers, the big sprints back to the rolling screener. This recovery sprint is the whole coverage — a jogging big gives up a dunk.
howTo.title: Sprint back to the roller

howTo.detail: Behind the play, the weak-side defenders are in rotation: one tags the roller, the others sink into gaps. The hedge only works if three players rotate behind it.
howTo.title: Weak side rotates behind the hedge

title: Hedging Ball Screens
whatIsIt: A hedge is an aggressive ball screen coverage where the screener's defender jumps out hard on the ball handler — 'showing' high above the screen — to stop the ball, then sprints back to the rolling screener. It is a temporary double-team designed to disrupt the pick & roll's timing.

The hedge buys the on-ball defender time to recover while blowing up the offense's rhythm. When it works, the ball handler is stuck 25 feet from the basket with nowhere to go. When it fails — a soft hedge, a slow recovery — it gives up the easiest dunk of the game to the rolling big.
whyItMatters: Hedging is the coverage you reach for when you need to take the ball out of a great player's hands. It is disruptive by design and can swing momentum in a close game. But it demands a mobile big, perfect timing, and three teammates rotating behind it — which is why it is a change-up weapon, not an every-possession diet.
